column2: Where do I find all my montage, sound, retouching and layout projects?
column3: Lists → 🛠️ Editing tools: one tab per tool (🎬 Video montage, 🎧 Sound, 🎚️ Photo retouching, 📐 Layout). Search by name, sort (newest, oldest, A → Z, Z → A), open, rename (✎) or delete (🗑) a project, or start a new one.

column2: How do I rename, resize or change the format of several images (or documents) at once?
column3: Lists → 🛠️ Editing tools → “⚙️ Batch processing” → “＋ New process”: a kind of Automator. 1. The files: “🖼 Choose from media…” (several at once, with search and filters) or drag them from the computer: images, documents (Word, LibreOffice, RTF, Markdown, text, web page; PDF read-only), spreadsheets (Excel, LibreOffice, CSV) and sounds. 2. The actions, as stacked cards that you order with ⠿ (or Alt + ↑ / ↓), switch off with the toggle, duplicate (⧉) or remove (×): Rename (a text, a sequence 001, 002…, the date, the title, the person or the place, find / replace, capitals, without accents), Resize (longest side, width, height, percentage, without enlarging), Crop, rotate, mirror, Black and white, Watermark, Change format (JPG, PNG, WebP, AVIF; .docx, .odt, .rtf, .md, .html, .txt; .xlsx, .ods, .csv; MP3, WAV, FLAC), Quality and size, Erase metadata (GPS position…), Tags and person, Combine into one PDF. 3. “Here is what will happen” shows each name, size and format before → after; choose the result (new version of the media item, the original staying in its versions; copy in the media; or ⤓ a ZIP) then “▶ Run”. In the database, “↶ Undo” puts everything back as before. Keep your chains in “💾 Saved recipes” (ready-made sets: Photos for the web, Rename in sequence, Scans to PDF…).

column2: Why does Retouch not show “Separate copy” and “Save without showing it”?
column3: These buttons are for photos in the database: the retouch becomes a version of the photo, the original being kept. For an empty canvas or an imported photo, there is no original to keep: “🖼 Save the image in Media” and “⤓ Download” are enough, and “💾 Save the project” keeps the layers so you can continue.

column2: Where do I put the Retouch tool column?
column3: Settings → “Montage, retouching, layout and sound” → 🎚️ Photo retouching: the tool column (➤ ⬚ ◯ 🪄 ⌗ 🖌 T…) next to the image, far left or far right, and the panel (Settings, Layers…) on the right or left. Then “Save”.

column2: How do I order or hide the buttons of the layout workshop?
column3: In the workshop, “⚙️ Customise” (top right), or Settings → “Montage, retouching, layout and sound” → Buttons and options → Editor “📐 Layout”: top menus, ↶ ↷, tools of the left column, tabs of the right panel and bottom bar, to tick and order with ↑ ↓. Open the workshop once so that the list fills up.

column2: How do I make layer groups in Retouch?
column3: Layers → “＋ Group” (or Layer → New group), or “Group” (⌘G) to put the chosen layer into a new group. A group can contain layers and other groups, as many levels as you like. The simplest: grab the ⠿ handle of a row and drag it — above or below another item, onto the middle of a group’s row (or onto “empty group”) to put it inside, onto the Photo row to put it right at the bottom. Also: the 📁 menu of each row, ↑ ↓ for the order, ▾ to fold a group. A group has its own visibility, opacity, lock and mask. ✕ on a group deletes it but keeps everything it contains.

column2: How do I put settings or filters in a layer (adjustment layer)?
column3: Layers → “＋ Adjustment” (or, at the top of the Settings and Filters tabs, “＋ in an adjustment layer”): the sliders, the curve and the filters then adjust that layer (the banner at the top says what you are adjusting; “adjust the photo” to go back). It acts on everything below it; tick “only on …” so that it only affects the layer or group just below (like a Photoshop clipping mask). Put in a group, it only affects that group. It can be masked, dosed (opacity) and hidden like a layer.

column2: How do I start from a blank image in Retouch?
column3: Lists → Media → “Retouch” → “⬜ Blank canvas”: choose the size (screen, square, A4, postcard or your own) and the background (white, transparent or a colour). The canvas is added to Media and opens in Retouch, ready for layers, text and shapes.

column2: How do I crop or straighten a photo in Retouch?
column3: Tool ⌗ (C): drag the handles of the frame or draw a new one, choose proportions (square, 4:3, A4…), rotate with “Straighten”, then “✓ Confirm” (or Enter). Escape cancels. Select menu → “Crop to selection” crops as tightly as possible.

column2: How do I hide part of a layer without erasing it (mask)?
column3: Layers → 🎭 on the layer (or the photo): a mask is added and the brush paints into it, ⬛ to hide, ⬜ to show. Click the layer thumbnail to go back to the layer. “invert the mask”, “remove the mask”, or Select → “Mask” to make one from the selection.

column2: How do I copy a whole area with the clone stamp?
column3: Select the area (⬚ ◯ ➰ ✒︎ 🪄), take the clone stamp 🧬 and drag: a copy of the area lands where you let go. Without a selection, the stamp copies with a brush from the chosen spot (🎯 or ⌥ + click).

column2: How do I write or draw shapes on a photo?
column3: Tool T: click, type, Enter (bold, italic, white outline, computer fonts). Tool ⬜: rectangle, rounded rectangle, ellipse, line or arrow, empty or filled (⇧: square, circle, right angle). With ➤ you move them, ⌫ deletes them, double-click a text to rewrite it.

column2: What filters does Retouch have?
column3: ✨ Filters tab (or Filter menu): blur, noise reduction, sharpness, clarity, grain and vignette, applied after the settings, also on the full-size saved image.

column2: How do I set up the layout of boards (toolbar, inspector)?
column3: Settings → Boards → “Menus and options” tab → “🧭 Board layout”: toolbar at the top, bottom or side, inspector on the right or left, button size, title shown or not. The ⚙️ button in a board leads straight there.

column2: How do I edit a block of a note on a subject?
column3: The block’s ✎ flips it over, like a dashboard widget: title, width (1, 1/2, 1/3, 1/4, 2/3, 3/4: you see it straight away), colour and content, then Save or Cancel. “＋ Block” adds a card at the bottom of the note, already flipped over to its settings.

column2: How do I hide the empty lines of a record’s Identity block?
column3: At the bottom of the Identity block: “Hide on this record” or “Hide on all” (and “Show…” to go back). The setting for all records is also in Settings → Appearance → record blocks.

column2: How do I hide lists in the Lists menu?
column3: Lists → “Reorder” (bottom left): it takes you to Settings → “Menus, column and lists” → “Lists” tab. The eye on each row hides or shows the list; drag or use ↑ ↓ for the order.

column2: How do I assemble sounds from scratch?
column3: Lists → 🎧 Audio → “🎬 Montage”: choose a first sound, then “＋ Add a sound…”, cut, fades, volume… “Save” makes it a new sound in the list.

column2: How do I add criteria to a distribution (Charts → Statistics)?
column3: Under “From … to … · Limit · Sex”, “＋ Criterion” adds as many criteria as you like, the same as in My lists and the Chart editor: name, occupation, tag, place, within … km of, had a marriage, number of children, my ancestors (Sosa), without source… The “not” box reverses a criterion, 🗑 removes it, “↺ Reset to default” removes them all. The statistic then only counts the records kept (and their events).

column2: How do I see who is behind a bar of a distribution?
column3: Click the bar (or column): a window shows the people counted, with a search, sorting by name or birth and a CSV export — as for a chart of your own. This works for surnames, first names, places and countries of birth, marriage and death, sexes, years of birth and death and age at death.

column2: How do I choose the starting filters of all distributions?
column3: On a distribution, “⚙️ Default settings of distributions”: set the years, limit, sex and criteria, then “⭐ Keep these filters as default for all”. They are used at the start of each distribution; “↺ Back to default filters” puts them back, “No more default setting” starts again from all the data.

column2: How do I keep all my app settings, or move them to another computer?
column3: Settings → Appearance, at the very bottom → “💾 Saved settings: the whole app”: “＋ Save current settings” and a name keep all the settings (appearance, lists and columns, your own charts and tabs, widgets, boards, animals, books, shortcuts…). “Apply” goes back to them (the screen reloads), ⋯ → “Export” makes a file of them, “⤒ Import” takes it up on another computer. Your data is never touched; what targets a specific record (root person, a record’s exception) and what is specific to this computer are not kept.

column2: Do saved settings keep Designs to choose from, portraits, Accessibility and Simple mode?
column3: Yes. “💾 Saved settings: Appearance” keeps everything about appearance: the design, Designs to choose from, portraits, the left column, menus, colours… “💾 Saved settings: the whole app” also keeps Accessibility, Simple mode settings and, for each list, its sort and the List or Cards view (not what you typed in the search). Never included, even in an exported file: the code to leave Simple mode, the person watching, hidden photos, the backup folder. A setting saved before these new features puts them back “As before”, without touching the Simple mode code; an old setting that contained the font, the dashboard or sets from Designs to choose from applies without error, those parts are simply ignored. An imported file is checked: anything unknown or damaged is left out.

column2: How do I keep or share my layout?
column3: Settings → Appearance → “💾 Saved settings: Appearance”: give a name to the current settings (design, menus shown or hidden and their order, blocks, colours…), go back to them in one click, or send the file to another user who imports it in the same place.

column2: How do I show the tree without the risk of it being changed?
column3: View-only mode (padlock at the top right) blocks any change; you leave it with your password.
